reason: The rocky world is central to the first goal, so placing it in its star's disk seems like a useful start.
expectation: I expect to position or follow the moon-bearing world within the disk, potentially setting up its encounter with the remaining stones.

alternatives.reason: The fragments and projectiles may address the material among the planets, but I chose to follow the rocky world first.

effect: The rocky world's encounter completed the first goal; I can now follow the remaining material.
reaction: The widened view makes it clear the moon-bearing world remains part of the same system.
reason: The fragments and projectiles seem relevant to the material left among the planets.
expectation: I expect another collision to change or redistribute the fragments, though the outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The exposed dust may also address the remaining goal, but I want to follow the fragments first.

effect: The collisions left debris between the planets, following a different path from the rubble world; the remaining action may address material returned outside.
reaction: The contrast between the two fates of the fragments is clear.
reason: This is the only offered gameplay action, and it follows the exposed dust.
expectation: I expect the exposed inner disk to change or move the dust-bearing gas, though its destination is uncertain.

effect: The exposed gas and dust return to the surrounding nursery, completing the final goal and connecting the system back to the galactic encounter.
reaction: The return of birth material to the wider surroundings is a satisfying closing connection.

mostWorthwhile.text: Returning disk material to the nursery was most worthwhile because it connected the planetary system to the wider story.

leastWorthwhile.text: Following the rocky world through the remaining stones felt less involved: the encounter and widened view happened in one action.

surprise.text: I didn't expect the exposed gas and dust to escape the disk and return to the nursery.

arbitrary.text: The final action's destination wasn't clear beforehand, although the result explained how radiation and drag affected the material.

continue.text: Yes, I'd continue for another chapter to see how the returned material participates in the wider galactic encounter, though the fast menu makes the choices fairly straightforward.
